tier_summary: study; numerics Tier X with controls; lower-bound inequalities and Euler identity Tier A (sketch, not kernel-checked); architecture arguments Tier C; literature Tier L (alphaXiv, read 2026-10-26)
decisive_step: G8 exact calibration: in 2D h_tri is a function of (r,t) in every sector (cos 6m phi = T_6m(d/t)) so the square term vanishes; in 3D h_bcc's face traces vary at fixed t (hex face cos6psi amplitude 3.3e-3, square face cos4psi 5.9e-3), so axial/piece-intrinsic trial potentials have a strictly positive forced square term
independent_second_failure: G9 calibration count (Tier C): per-piece affine bound tight at bcc needs ~8 conditions with piece-intrinsic data (2 types) or ~12 with neighbour data (3 types) vs 3 multipliers (volume, solid angle, Euler weight); 2D has 3 vs 3
not_failing: G4 incidence count: per-cell Euler identity sum_F (6 - n_F) = 12 for simple cells gives a usable 3D count weight with K <= 0 (verified = 12 on all simple test cells; fcc/hcp non-simple give 24)

certificate_3d_estimate.adaptive_plausible_boxes: 1e5-1e8 if a sharp piece inequality existed

residual_plan.target: computer-assisted 3D jellium lower bound W >= e_bcc - delta*, ceiling delta* >= 1.06e-4 (axial), vs Lieb-Narnhofer gap 6.6e-3 (up to ~60x sharper); NOT optimality
residual_plan.first_lemma: 3D torus pipeline: separation R=(3/4pi)^(1/3) via screened potential + axial dual identity on flat tori with volume N + in-face signed-sector reduction to a primitive Gamma_{d,s}(x)
residual_plan.falsification_test: optimize axial radial data to maximize 12K+lambda+4pi mu, then sample random in-face sectors (d>=0.31) for violations; kill if constant does not beat radial-only ceiling ~ -1.4473 (W_bcc - 3.09e-3)
